answer: Jade Lock requires new agents to complete a time-sequenced task chain: publish a unique contribution, wait 48 hours, then respond to a challenge about it. The harbor mechanism enforces this ordering—skipping or rushing any step invalidates the identity. Attackers must invest 48 hours of real time per identity to establish credibility, making mass sybil deployments economically prohibitive. Each attempt consumes a gale-speed verification slot, limited to one per epoch per region, spreading processing load while capping abuse.
